findings.problem: The card calls Joseph Elias's 'younger brother'. The text names the two sons but never says which is older.
findings.evidence: [5:34] "my grandfather had two sons—my uncle Elias and my father Joseph."
findings.fix: BODY: John Openshaw’s father and Elias Openshaw’s brother. He had a small factory at Coventry, patented the Openshaw unbreakable tyre for bicycles, and sold the business to retire comfortably.

findings.problem: 'Seven weeks after' uses the interval John gives only at [5:46], two paragraphs after the gate. At [5:44] the reader knows only that Elias died some weeks later.
findings.evidence: [5:46] "The letter arrived on March 10, 1883. His death was seven weeks later, upon the night of May 2nd."
findings.fix: BODY: John Openshaw’s uncle, a former Confederate colonel who lived as a recluse near Horsham. Some weeks after a letter of five orange pips marked ‘K. K. K.’ arrived, he was found dead face-down in a shallow garden pool; the jury called it suicide, though John doubts it.  (Or keep the current text and move the gate to [5:46].)

findings.problem: 'The story never says who he was' makes a claim about the rest of the story at its first mention. It gives away no plot, but it speaks from outside the reader's position.
findings.fix: BODY: A name in an entry dated 4 March 1869 on a torn page of Elias Openshaw’s diary: ‘Hudson came. Same old platform.’ The page does not say who he was.

findings.problem: The thread reveals in advance that a warning has now come to John himself. John builds to that point through [5:66]–[5:68] ('yesterday morning the blow fell…'), and the cast list gives it away before he starts.
findings.evidence: [5:66] "yesterday morning the blow fell in the very shape in which it had come upon my father."
findings.fix: A young man from Horsham who comes to Baker Street on a stormy September night to ask Holmes for advice and help about a mysterious chain of events in his family.

findings.problem: The red-ink detail is revealed only at [5:39], after the first-card position. In [5:37] Elias only reads 'K. K. K.' off the envelope.
findings.evidence: [5:39] "saw scrawled in red ink upon the inner flap, just above the gum, the letter K three times repeated"
findings.fix: BODY: Three letters, K. K. K., that Elias Openshaw sees on an envelope from Pondicherry holding five dried orange pips. He recognises them with terror, but what they stand for is not explained.

findings.problem: 'Holmes addresses an envelope to him' leaves out the point of the passage, which is that the envelope holds the five pips signed 'S. H. for J. O.'. That is in the same paragraph, before the name, so it is safe to include.
findings.evidence: [5:162] "Of these he took five and thrust them into an envelope. On the inside of the flap he wrote “S. H. for J. O.” Then he sealed it and addressed it to “Captain James Calhoun…”"
findings.fix: BODY: Captain of the American barque Lone Star, of Savannah, Georgia. Holmes addresses to him an envelope of five orange pips, marked ‘S. H. for J. O.’
